subject: Confirmation: Do you train models on customer data? + deletion workflow
messages:
From: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@acme.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai; security@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-12 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Model training / retention confirmation + questionnaire attached

Hi Lauren,

As part of Acme's procurement security review we're validating that vendor platforms do not use customer-provided data to train or improve models unless explicitly contracted. Please confirm: do you use customer production data to train models?

Also, can you outline your data retention defaults (logs, request bodies, insights) and the process for a customer-initiated deletion request (including expected timeline and audit evidence)? I've attached our security questionnaire (key pages 7-9).

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lewis
Senior Security Engineer, Acme Corp
Attachment: security-questionnaire_acme.pdf (application/pdf, 312KB)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-12 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Model training / retention confirmation + questionnaire attached

Aditya, Vivek — forwarding Acme's questionnaire. Short deadline: procurement wants an answer and deletion workflow description by EOD PT tomorrow. Can you help me draft the official response? Key points to cover: explicit statement on training usage, default retention windows for request/response payloads, logs retention, immediate deletion steps and evidence (what we can hand them).

I suggest we include the deletion playbook PDF and SOC2 excerpt. Aditya, can you confirm whether any telemetry with PII could persist in internal monitoring for more than 30 days? Vivek, any region/residency nuances we should call out for their EU subsidiaries?

Thanks — LB

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-12 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Model training / retention confirmation + questionnaire attached

Lauren — draft points below (technical):

- Training usage: Redwood does NOT use customer production data to continually train or update our public models. Customer request/response payloads are not injected into model training corpora used for improving model weights. We offer an explicit opt-in program for partners who want data to be used for research/model improvement under strict contracts; that is not enabled by default.

- Retention defaults: request/response payloads for the hosted API are retained for 30 days by default to support abuse detection and billing reconciliation. Metadata (timestamps, token counts, model id, non-personal routing info) is retained for 90 days. Audit logs and billing records are retained per contractual terms (can be extended for Dedicated/Private).

- Deletion workflow: upon an authenticated deletion request we: (1) mark customer data for deletion, (2) remove request/response payloads from hot stores, (3) schedule background purge jobs to delete replicas within 72 hours, (4) record an immutable deletion event in the audit ledger. For Dedicated and Private customers we can provide deletion confirmation exports.

- Evidence: we can provide a signed deletion manifest (CSV) listing request IDs, deletion timestamps, and audit ledger hash. For enterprise customers we can arrange a live walkthrough and retention configuration export.

- Edge cases: archived backups are on a weekly cadence; backup retention is 90 days by default and deletion from backups occurs on the next backup cycle (we include this in the manifest).

I'll attach a short playbook and SOC2 excerpt. Vivek — anything to add on residency / EU special-cases?

— Aditya

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-12 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Model training / retention confirmation + questionnaire attached

Adding regional nuance: for customers who select a data residency region (e.g., eu-west-1) all primary request/response storage and KV caches remain in that region and deletion jobs operate regionally. For cross-region failover we replicate metadata only; we do not replicate payloads unless customer enables cross-region DR. In the EU we also offer an extended deletion SLA (48 hours) and can provide exportable deletion proof tied to the customer's key in KMS.

I'll attach a residency appendix to the playbook.

— Vivek

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@acme.com>, security@acme.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-13 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model training / retention confirmation + questionnaire attached

Hi Sara — thanks for sending the questionnaire. Apologies for the short turnaround; below is our official position and the attachments referenced.

Short answer on training: Redwood does NOT use customer production data to train, fine-tune, or improve our public models by default. Any use of customer data for model improvement requires an explicit contractual opt-in with documented scope and controls.

Retention and deletion (summary):
- Default request/response payload retention: 30 days (hot storage)
- Metadata retention: 90 days
- Backups: weekly snapshots, retained 90 days; deletion from backups occurs on the next snapshot cycle and is included in deletion manifests
- Deletion process: authenticated request -> mark for deletion -> purge hot copies (within 72 hours) -> background purge of replicas -> immutable audit ledger entry -> provide signed deletion manifest upon request

Regional notes: if you choose EU residency we keep payloads and caches in-region; deletion jobs and manifests are region-specific. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can adjust retention windows and provide tailored deletion proofs and key separation (KMS/HSM).

Evidence / attachments provided: redwood-deletion-playbook.pdf (step-by-step deletion flow + manifest sample), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 controls excerpt). We can provide a signed CSV manifest for a sample deletion set and schedule a short walkthrough with engineering if you'd like.

Please let me know if Acme needs: (1) a signed statement on the opt-in-only policy, (2) a deletion manifest for a specific dataset, or (3) a live session to review logs and audit entries. Happy to set up a call — propose Thu 05/15 09:00 PT if that works.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of GTM Security & Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-deletion-playbook.pdf (application/pdf, 160KB), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (application/pdf, 120KB)
